subtopics.title: The Hyperbola — Branches, Asymptotes and Restrictions

questions.question: For y = 8/x, the asymptotes are:
The domain of y = 8/x is:
options: All real x except x = 0, because division by zero is undefined

questions.question: A hyperbola of the form y = a/x + q has:
options: NO y-intercept, because x = 0 is excluded from the domain

questions.question: The branches of y = −8/x lie in which quadrants?

questions.question: For y = 8/x + 2, the horizontal asymptote is:
The range of y = 8/x + 2 is:
The x-intercept of y = 8/x + 2 is:

subtopics.title: The Exponential Graph — Growth, Decay and Its Asymptote

questions.question: For y = 3ˣ, the value at x = −2 is:
The range of y = 3ˣ is:
options: y > 0 strictly, because 3 to any power is positive but never zero

questions.question: Every graph of the form y = bˣ passes through:
options: (0; 1), because b to the power 0 is 1 for every base

questions.question: Why may the base b not equal 1?
options: Because the graph would have two branches
Because 1 to any power is 1, giving a horizontal line rather than an exponential curve
Because the range would become negative

questions.question: For y = 3ˣ − 9, the asymptote and y-intercept are:
The x-intercept of y = 3ˣ − 9 is:
For y = −3ˣ + 3, the range is:
options: y < 3, because a positive quantity is always subtracted from 3

questions.question: Which is an exhibit from the error museum?
options: Drawing the asymptote dashed before the curve
Drawing a curve that touches or crosses its own asymptote
Writing the range of y = 3ˣ as y > 0

questions.question: A fixed R240 pitch fee split between 6 players costs each:
The two impossibilities in the shared-fee story become which two features of the graph?
options: Two asymptotes — the share never reaches zero, and you cannot share among nobody

questions.question: From 2 to 3 players each saves R40, but from 11 to 12 the saving is barely R2. On the graph this appears as:
options: A curve that rises steeply throughout
A curve that drops steeply at first and then flattens out

questions.question: Why does the shared-fee curve never meet the up-and-down axis?
options: Because you can never put zero in — sharing among zero people does not exist
Because the curve has two branches
Because the numbers become too large to plot

questions.question: One person with the meme, then two, then four, then eight — this is growth by:
Running the doubling backwards gives a half, a quarter, an eighth… The point is that:
options: You can halve forever and always have something left, so the curve never lands on the bottom line
The pattern breaks after ten rounds

questions.question: Every curve in this family shares one free point, because:
options: The curve is symmetrical about the y-axis
Anything to the power zero is one, so the crossing on the up-and-down axis is at 1

questions.question: A second-hand phone losing half its resale value each year gives a curve that:
options: Starts high on the left and glides down toward the bottom line, never touching it
Crosses the bottom line and continues below it

subtopics.title: Asymptote First — the Routine and the Traps

questions.question: The sketching routine begins with:
options: Drawing the dashed line the curve will not touch

questions.question: For a graph shifted down nine, writing 'asymptote at zero' is wrong because:
options: Zero can never be an asymptote
The untouchable line moves with the graph — here it is nine units below zero
The graph has no asymptote once it is shifted

questions.question: Solving 3ˣ − 9 = 0 for the crossing of the flat axis gives:
The 'ground floor or upstairs?' question separates:
options: y = x², which turns around, from y = 3ˣ, which never turns
